final_candidates.decision_summary: Highest LOF-proxy score (0.827) in the pool with low alanine frequency among homologs, indicating a conserved, functionally critical Arg in the C-terminal TM region. Charge removal is expected to disrupt transport while alanine preserves local packing and abundance.

Second-highest LOF proxy (0.802); this conserved acidic residue near TM11 likely participates in substrate recognition/binding, and removing the carboxylate should abolish transport without grossly destabilizing the helix.
Strong LOF proxy (0.756) and very low alanine frequency in homologs (0.043) support functional importance of this TM aromatic residue, plausibly in the substrate translocation pathway.

stop_reason.detail: Top-3 ranking is stable across available evidence dimensions and remaining tools offer no additional decision-relevant signal.

history.rationale: Conserved acidic residue in the C-terminal transmembrane region; neutralizing Asp should remove cation/substrate coordination while Ala is minimally destabilizing.
Aspartate in TM11-adjacent conserved OCT motif region; charge removal likely disrupts substrate translocation while alanine preserves backbone geometry and folding.
Second-highest LOF proxy (0.802); acidic residue near TM11 likely involved in substrate binding; alanine swap expected to ablate transport while preserving fold.
Aromatic residue in the conserved N-terminal TM pocket likely contributes to substrate recognition; Ala removes the side chain without introducing charge.
Aromatic residue in the central cavity-facing region (TM5 area); aromatic cage residues are implicated in cation binding in OCTs, so Ala may abolish transport.
Moderate LOF proxy (0.635); retained as backup but demoted below R485A/Y220A.
Tyrosine near the W216 pocket plausibly participates in organic-cation π/polar interactions; Ala is expected to impair transport more than folding.
Tyr near W216 in the putative substrate pocket; conservative cavity disruption candidate.
Strong LOF proxy (0.756) and very low A frequency among homologs (0.043) indicate functional importance; aromatic residue in TM region supports substrate-pathway role.
Aspartate in a middle TM/loop transition could support cation translocation; charge removal is a classic LOF strategy with moderate abundance risk.
Negative charge in TM7/8 region; acidic residues are common transport-critical determinants in SLC22 family.
Alphamissense classifies as benign (0.108); unlikely to abolish transport.

rejection.reason: Alphamissense classifies as benign (0.108); unlikely to abolish transport.

history.rationale: Basic residue in the intracellular/TM region may stabilize substrate or conformational state; Ala neutralizes charge while retaining small hydrophobic packing.
Arginine near TM11 exit; guanidinium–substrate interactions plausible, Ala removes them.
Highest alphamissense LOF score (0.827) in the pool; conserved Arg in the C-terminal TM region, low mutant frequency supports strong functional disruption.
Glu-to-Gln preserves size and polarity but removes negative charge, potentially reducing cation transport with limited structural perturbation.
Conservative charge-removal mutation with high LOF proxy (0.721); zero Q frequency among homologs supports functional importance of the carboxylate.
Glycine in a tight GG-containing segment likely enables helix flexibility for the transport cycle; Ser restricts backbone motion but carries some folding risk.
Benign LOF proxy (0.177) and high S frequency in homologs; unlikely to disrupt function.

rejection.reason: Benign LOF proxy (0.177) and high S frequency in homologs; unlikely to disrupt function.

history.rationale: Phenylalanine near a TM packing face may couple substrate binding to helix movement; Ala can impair gating, though abundance effects are less certain.
Benign LOF proxy (0.283); insufficient evidence for transport ablation.
